svg.title: The three levels of electronic signature under eIDAS
svg.desc: Three ascending steps: simple, advanced and qualified electronic signatures, each listing what it requires and its legal effect.
svg.text: Regulation (EU) 910/2014 (eIDAS), Articles 3 and 25. Each level includes everything below it.

g.text: LEVEL 1
Simple electronic signature
WHAT IT IS
Any electronic data attached to a document
and used to sign: a typed name, a scanned
image, a “click to accept”.
LEGAL EFFECT
Cannot be rejected only for being electronic.
Weight as evidence is decided case by case. Art. 25(1)
LEVEL 2
Advanced electronic signature
WHAT IT REQUIRES
1. Uniquely linked to the signer
2. Capable of identifying the signer
3. Created with means under the signer’s
sole control
4. Any later change to the data is detectable
HOW IT IS DONE IN PRACTICE
Public-key cryptography: a private key held by
the signer, a certificate from a certificate
authority binding the key to a name.
LEVEL 3
Qualified electronic signature
WHAT IT REQUIRES, ON TOP OF LEVEL 2
• A qualified certificate, issued by a
qualified trust service provider that a
national supervisor has listed on the
EU trusted lists
• The private key kept on a qualified
signature creation device (smart card,
token, or a certified remote HSM)
• The signer’s identity verified in person
or by an equivalent method before issue
LEGAL EFFECT
Equivalent to a handwritten signature.
Recognised in every EU member state.

svg.text: Seals (Art. 35) mirror signatures for legal persons such as companies and authorities; a qualified seal guarantees origin and integrity rather than a person’s consent.
